characters: Serwaa: a fourteen-year-old JHS 2 student in a clean white food-laboratory apron and hairnet, checking kitchen scales.
Nii: her thirteen-year-old classmate at the ICT lab computer, keen on spreadsheets, formulas, and charts.
Latifa: their fourteen-year-old group treasurer holding a neat enterprise ledger and calculator.
Madam Osei: the JHS Career Technology teacher in a crisp white coat inspecting portion weights.

notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.
Pronounce spreadsheet formulas, geometric terms, and security acronyms clearly and unhurriedly.

BECE High-Frequency Error Guardrail: Directly prevents omitting the leading equals sign (=) in formulas and dividing profit by selling price instead of cost price.

teacherGuide.overview: Unites Career Technology food production and costing with Computing spreadsheet modelling and BECE commercial arithmetic (ratios, linear break-even equations, and profit percentage on cost price).
learningGoals: Write dynamic spreadsheet formulas using =, cell references, and functions.
Scale ingredient quantities accurately using ratios and enforce cross-contamination rules.
Calculate percentage profit on cost and solve linear equations to find break-even sales.

subjectLinks.link: Electronic Spreadsheets: Cell references, formulas, functions, and charts

subjectLinks.link: Food hygiene, portion control, costing, and small business management

beforeReading: Write =4+3*2 and =(4+3)*2 on the board: ask learners what a spreadsheet will display in each cell and why.
whileReading: Pause on Page 3 and emphasise why GH¢ 80 profit on GH¢ 320 cost is 25%, NOT 20%.
afterReading: Build the exact 6-row meat-pie budget in Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc, or Google Sheets and test changing flour prices.
discussion: Why do many small food businesses run out of cash when owners spend total sales revenue without separating initial Cost Price capital?
reflection: How can accurate weighing and spreadsheet tracking prevent waste in a family or school enterprise?

mathsExtension.task: A recipe for 20 meat pies requires 1,250 g of flour and 500 g of margarine. How many kilograms of flour and margarine are required to bake 100 meat pies?
mathsExtension.answer: Scale factor = 100 ÷ 20 = 5. Flour = 1,250 g × 5 = 6,250 g = 6.25 kg. Margarine = 500 g × 5 = 2,500 g = 2.5 kg.

support: Provide a paper 4×6 spreadsheet grid labelled Columns A–D and Rows 1–6 so learners trace cell coordinates visually before typing.
stretch: With total sales entered in cell D8, add the logical formula =IF(D8>D6, "PROFIT", "LOSS") to display enterprise status automatically.
